message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance as international hubs:

| Airport (IATA) | City / State | Passenger Traffic (2019) | Notes |
|----------------|--------------|--------------------------|-------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International (ATL)** | Atlanta, GA | ~107 million | Largest by passenger volume; major connecting hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| **Los Angeles International (LAX)** | Los Angeles, CA | ~88 million | Key gateway to Asia and Latin America; major hub for American Airlines and Delta. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International (ORD)** | Chicago, IL | ~84 million | One of the busiest airports worldwide; hub for United and American. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International (DFW)** | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | ~75 million | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| **Denver International (DEN)** | Denver, CO | ~69 million | Hub for United and Southwest; largest airport by land area in the U.S. |
| **John F. Kennedy International (JFK)** | New York City, NY | ~62 million | Primary hub for United and JetBlue; major gateway to Europe. |
| **San Francisco International (SFO)** | San Francisco, CA | ~57 million | Hub for United and a key gateway to Asia. |
| **Seattle‑Tacoma International (SEA)** | Seattle, WA | ~48 million | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| **Miami International (MIA)** | Miami, FL | ~45 million | Major hub for American and a key gateway to Latin America. |
| **Orlando International (MCO)** | Orlando, FL | ~44 million | Major hub for Southwest; high seasonal traffic due to tourism. |

These airports serve as major hubs for airlines, have extensive international connections, and handle the highest volumes of passengers in the United States.
